question.text: In an IPO where the majority of the issue proceeds (excluding any offer-for-sale component) are NOT being used for capital expenditure, for how long is the minimum promoters' contribution locked-in from the date of allotment?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI ICDR Regulations (NISM-Series-IX workbook, p.153), the minimum promoters' contribution (20% of post-issue capital) is locked-in for 18 months from the later of (a) the date of commencement of commercial production or (b) the date of allotment. For the non-capex default case stated in this stem, the lock-in is therefore 18 months from allotment. The longer 3-year (36-month) lock-in applies only where the majority of the issue proceeds (excluding OFS) are deployed for capital expenditure. The Trap: Option C (36 months) is correct only under the capex-majority case — in the original ambiguous stem with no capex/non-capex framing, candidates could reasonably defend either 18 or 36 months. 12 months and 6 months do not correspond to the minimum promoters' contribution lock-in at all; 6 months is the lock-in for promoter holdings in excess of the minimum 20%. Note: The original stem did not specify whether the issue proceeds were earmarked majority-capex or not. Because SEBI ICDR provides 18 months as the default but 3 years where the majority of proceeds (excluding OFS) are for capex, both 18-month and 36-month answers were defensible. The stem has been tightened to the explicit non-capex case so that 18 months is the unique answer. Source: NISM-Series-IX Merchant Banking workbook, p.153.
